methods.label: Separate driving time from total time
methods.explanation:
The stop contributes to the trip time but adds no distance. It lasts \(20/60=1/3\) hour, leaving
\[
3-\frac13=\frac83
\]
hours of driving.

Since \(t\) is the time driven before the stop, the time driven afterward is \(\frac83-t\). Using distance equals speed times time, the first part covers \(80t\) kilometers and the second covers \(100(\frac83-t)\) kilometers. Their sum is \(250\), so the required equation is
\[
80t+100\left(\frac83-t\right)=250,
\]
choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses a minutes-to-hours conversion and a one-variable distance equation; solving the equation is not required.
